clue.text: Support a student and offer cash

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
L is a learner, the student driver's plate
to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: Someone backs a student financially and hands over money.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is the currency a creditor must accept, i.e. ready money.

clue.text: £1 note — credit application to face!

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for the pound sign
the numeral one looks like the letter I
PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
tick is British slang for credit, buying on tick

explanation.surface: A pound note, borrowing and applying for credit with brazen cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application to face' reads like brazenness in asking for credit, but it is makeup put on the face. 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip colour is a cosmetic applied to the mouth, part of the face.

clue.text: Leave rum cocktail with one who likes food

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of rum are mixed

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a rum cocktail in favour of a hearty eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a lover of good eating, a glutton or epicure.

clue.text: In a superior way, is fond of pools

indicators.note: spoken in an affected upper-class accent, so the word is heard with a drawled vowel

parts.note: likes means is fond of

explanation.surface: Someone haughtily expresses a fondness for swimming pools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a superior way' signals a plummy upper-class accent, in which the vowel of LIKES is drawn out to sound like LAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakes are bodies of standing water, so large pools.

clue.text: Account for Times found in eastern pampas

indicators.note: the times sign is discovered sitting within the eastern plain

parts.note: the pampas is a vast South American plain
X is the multiplication or times sign

explanation.surface: A rancher justifies the hours spent out on the eastern grasslands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper here but the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to give a reason or account for it.

clue.text: Dreadful initial losing streak — couldn't be more gloomy

indicators.note: only the opening letter of dreadful is taken
losing suggests the word streak losing its shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler bemoans a terrible start to a run of defeats that leaves them utterly downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing streak' reads as one phrase, but 'losing' rearranges STREAK into ARKEST, placed after the D from 'Dreadful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of dark, used for the gloomiest mood or outlook.

clue.text: Ray's measures for Greens not negotiable

indicators.note: something negotiable can be reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Green Party policies on radiation are presented as fixed and not up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not negotiable' reads as 'fixed', but 'negotiable' rearranges GREENS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old unit of X-ray and gamma-ray exposure, so radiation is measured in them.

clue.text: Daring to go topless and getting on

indicators.note: the top, or first letter, of the synonym for daring is removed

parts.note: bold means daring

explanation.surface: A daring older person decides to sunbathe without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on in years is aged.

clue.text: One might foresee boat not starting

indicators.note: the first letter of the boat's name does not begin the word

parts.note: a coracle is a small round Welsh boat

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller predicts that a boat will fail to start.
explanation.walkthrough: A CORACLE is a small round wicker boat used in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a prophet or seer who predicts the future.

clue.text: European elan captivating province

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: dash means elan, flair
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A continental's flair charms a whole region.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province' in the UK, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane is a European, from Denmark.

clue.text: Bottle party began by accident

indicators.note: the party's letter comes at the start, so the rest follows it

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for party
luck means chance or accident

explanation.surface: A party at which a bottle was opened came about by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang means nerve or courage, the same as spirit.

clue.text: China's new role? Panic

indicators.note: new tells us the letters take a new form, an anagram

explanation.surface: The Chinese state worries about its new international role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is fine pottery; 'new' rearranges ROLE PANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine ceramic ware, another name for porcelain.

clue.text: Newspaper to run property investment…

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A newspaper decides to back a property scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition needs 'property investment'; the print reads 'proper', a letter or two short.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is part-ownership of a holiday home, bought as a property stake.

clue.text: Accounts that ended with complex sale.

indicators.note: the end of the word that supplies its last letter
complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of sale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stories that finished with an elaborate sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are stories or narratives, i.e. accounts of events.

clue.text: To do with business

explanation.surface: A note on what a firm deals with.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means relate to or involve; as a noun, a firm or company.

clue.text: How one looked when a diet came off?

definitions.text: How one looked when a diet came off?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes their appearance after a successful diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges A DIET CAME; read whole, the clue describes how a dieter looks when the diet works.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin, as from severe dieting.

clue.text: They may be counted on after 10

definitions.text: They may be counted on after 10

parts.words: They may be counted on after 10
parts.note: once a child has counted to ten on their fingers, the next digits used are on the feet

explanation.surface: Things that can be relied upon after ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counted on' looks like 'relied on', but it means counting using them, as children use fingers up to ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits on the feet continue a count once the fingers run out.

clue.text: Call for retirement

parts.note: a military bugle call sounded at the end of the day and at funerals

explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed or death, not leaving a job: the bugle call ending a soldier's day and played at funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: This bugle call signals the close of the day in camp and is played at military funerals.

clue.text: Give aid to China after case of belligerence

indicators.note: the friend comes after the outer letters
the case is the outer shell, the first and last letters of belligerence

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, so china means friend

explanation.surface: One country helps China after a bout of aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so 'china' is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to act as a friend and help them.

clue.text: Call for some ice

explanation.surface: Someone asks for ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout out to someone is to hail them; hailstones are pellets of ice.

clue.text: Caerphilly cheese stuffed with fruit

indicators.note: the cheese words contain the answer packed inside them

explanation.surface: A Welsh cheese filled with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a crumbly Welsh cheese; the answer runs across 'CaerphilLY CHEESe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lychees are small sweet Asian fruits with rough red skins.

clue.text: Error in highway investment

parts.note: the M1 is a major British motorway, written MI
a stake is a share or investment

explanation.surface: A mistaken investment in a road project.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its 1 stands as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a blunder or slip, a wrong step.

clue.text: Remain confused by origin of rock salt

indicators.note: the letters of remain are muddled into a new order
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled by where rock salt comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock salt' reads as one thing, but 'salt' is the definition: an old salt is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, a seafarer.

clue.text: Put on a show and invests time in rising French artist

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, rising means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A French painter ascending in fame stages an exhibition and puts time into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns DEGAS into SAGED, and 'invests' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Staged means presented as a performance, as a play is put on.

clue.text: Quietly dressed and investigated

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
robed means dressed in a robe

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly got dressed and looked into things.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to examine or inquire thoroughly.

clue.text: Sailor, oddly, skin and bones

parts.note: tar is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of skin are taken

explanation.surface: A strange sailor who is just skin and bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle.

clue.text: Tradesman and nurse held captive

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a carer is someone who looks after or nurses another
pent means penned in, captive

explanation.surface: A tradesman and a nurse are held hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a woodworker, a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Stimulate the market? A lesson in holding it back

indicators.note: back tells us to read those letters in reverse
the run of words holds the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A trader asks whether a lesson will stimulate the market by holding it back.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'markET A LEsson'; 'back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with high spirits, so to excite or stimulate.

clue.text: Negotiator's turn to gamble with small Scottish town without pull

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
a bet is a gamble
wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the pull is taken away from the town

parts.note: taken as the word town
to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: A mediator takes a chance on a small Scottish town that lacks clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish town' reads as a place name, but 'Scottish' goes with 'small' (WEE) and 'without pull' takes TOW from TOWN to leave N.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who carries messages between parties.

clue.text: "Home is the sailor" (poem)

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A quotation of Stevenson's line 'Home is the sailor', from his poem Requiem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes R. L. Stevenson's epitaph 'Home is the sailor, home from sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling place, where one lives.

clue.text: Misfire — resentment has gone astray, gone astray

indicators.note: gone astray signals that the letters of gone wander off out of the resentment word, which is taken apart

parts.note: dudgeon is a feeling of offended resentment, as in high dudgeon

explanation.surface: A shot fails as anger goes off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone astray' says the letters of GONE are taken out of DUDGEON, the remaining letters giving the definition's word; the repeated phrase is a print duplication.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that fails to work, like a shell that does not explode.

clue.text: Bewildered Tories dined out

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians are confused after eating out.
explanation.definitionFit: Disoriented means having lost one's bearings, so confused.
